summary: Broad human pancreas coverage is plausible, but several state axes need targeted biological cleanup for healthy baseline pancreas.

issues.description: The module is labeled as zymogen load but is dominated by unfolded-protein-response and ER-stress genes rather than acinar digestive enzyme or zymogen markers.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename/reframe this as an acinar secretory-stress/UPR state, or replace the gene list and axis name with a nonredundant healthy acinar subtype/state if a true zymogen-load axis is intended.

issues.description: The module mixes healthy ductal ion/fluid transport genes with TFF/mucinous markers that are more suggestive of gastric/metaplastic or pathological ductal programs than healthy baseline pancreas.
issues.suggested_fix: Retune the module toward healthy ductal and centroacinar transport/secretion markers, keeping transport genes such as CFTR, SLC4A4, and AQP1 while avoiding TFF/metaplastic markers unless the axis is explicitly renamed as a metaplastic or stress state.

issues.description: Canonical pDCs may not score strongly on the monocyte/macrophage-biased myeloid_core gate, so the current gated axis can suppress a biologically valid pancreatic immune subtype.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a dendritic/APC gate that includes HLA/FLT3/IRF8/CST3 or add a separate pDC identity axis, while keeping pDC markers contrasted against cDC and monocyte/macrophage modules within an appropriate immune compartment.

issues.description: The ungated progenitor-to-mature-endocrine contrast uses genes shared by adult ductal/centroacinar and beta-cell programs, so without a developmental note it may not represent a clean expected healthy-pancreas axis.
issues.suggested_fix: Gate the axis to pancreatic epithelium and make the contrast explicitly immature/progenitor-like versus mature epithelial programs if broad age coverage is intended; otherwise retune it into a ductal/centroacinar progenitor-like state or replace it with mature compartment resolution.

out_of_scope: Adipocytes, neutrophils, and rare endocrine subtypes are not heavily represented, but this is acceptable unless the downstream dataset is known to include substantial peripancreatic fat or blood contamination.
Some overlap between marker modules is acceptable and not a structural issue by itself.
